transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-25
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM); Maya Torres (Sentinel Channel Lead), Evan Kim (Sentinel Alliances), Liam O'Connor (Sentinel AE)

Summary (auto): quick review of pipeline, call out of top deals, plan for two pilot benchmarks, security asks and next steps captured.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Moreno: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um let's do a quick roll call then we'll jump in, Priya you're good?
[00:08] Priya Shah: yep yep here, loud and clear.
[00:10] Jordan Lee: Jordan on my side, thanks.
[00:12] Maya Torres: Maya here from Sentinel.
[00:14] Evan Kim: Evan on the line.
[00:16] Liam O'Connor: Liam joining, sorry bit of background noise.
[00:18] Alex Moreno: cool, thanks, so agenda — pipeline review, identify top 4-6 co-sell qualifies, alignment on who owns next steps and then, uh, POC/benchmark asks. sound right?
[00:28] Maya Torres: yep that works, we wanted to call out a couple new opps that just came in from our healthcare vertical.
[00:34] Alex Moreno: perfect, Evan do you want to kick us off with the pipeline snapshot?
[00:39] Evan Kim: sure so quick snapshot, we have six joint opps right now that we think are co-sell ready: Aurora (large retail), Meridian Health (healthcare, high compliance), Zephyr Financial (mid-market finserv), Nova Logistics (supply chain), Orion Energy (utility), and Cascade Systems (SaaS). rough total ACV across the six is about $2.1M ARR if we close as projected, pipeline stage varies from early discovery to final procurement for one deal.
[00:58] Priya Shah: quick question about Aurora — what's the latency SLO they're asking for? I know retail use-case is latency sensitive.
[01:04] Liam O'Connor: Aurora's asking for sub-150ms p50 for the storefront recommendations and also they'd like offline batch embeddings for nightly retrain.
[01:12] Priya Shah: okay that puts them in the dedicated or at least reserved capacity conversation, because hosted might be a bit dicey at that SLA if volume spikes.
[01:20] Alex Moreno: agreed, we should price both motions and show cost delta. also this is where caching/prefix caching will help, but we should be explicit about the dedicated commitment we recommend.
[01:28] Maya Torres: and for Meridian Health, compliance is the big blocker — they need SOC2 plus data residency in EU and an on-prem option for certain de-identified datasets.
[01:37] Jordan Lee: that sounds like a Private deployment conversation — we can outline VPC/on-prem options, KMS integration and audit log flows. I'll capture the security asks.
[01:44] Evan Kim: on the Zephyr Financial opp, they're already evaluating a competitor — I think I heard Anthropic mentioned in their RFP, and one of their architects is leaning towards serverless options on AWS Bedrock to consolidate.
[01:54] Alex Moreno: okay we should map competitive differentiators there: performance/cost predictable on Dedicated, plus clearer rollout and fallback policies. Priya can help show latency and cost delta in a benchmark.
[02:03] Priya Shah: yeah I can run a quick perf run: two model variants, 1k token average, and show p50/p95 across hosted vs dedicated vs quantized private run. need access to a sample prompt set and a small corpus.
[02:13] Maya Torres: we can share redacted prompt sets for Aurora and Zephyr this week.
[02:17] Evan Kim: note — Zephyr also asked about SSO and SAML for end users and RBAC for admin ops.
[02:22] Priya Shah: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, and we have RBAC on the console. for Private, we can also map to customer AD via LDAP. we'll send the security sheet after call.
[02:31] Liam O'Connor: can you include KMS options — we need to be clear if we can bring our own key or if Redwood manages keys.
[02:36] Jordan Lee: yes BYOK supported through KMS/HSM integrations, we'll include diagrams.
[02:40] Alex Moreno: great, moving on — prioritization. we propose Aurora and Meridian as top two pilots: Aurora for performance/we need a dedicated motion and Meridian for Private/compliance. Does the Sentinel team agree?
[02:50] Maya Torres: yes those align with our internal priorities. Aurora has a Q1 rollout target, Meridian is Q2 but needs procurement prep now.
[02:57] Evan Kim: Meridian's stakeholders include privacy, legal, and infra — procurement timeline could be 8-12 weeks.
[03:04] Alex Moreno: noted. for Aurora — Liam, can you lead the joint POC outreach and coordinate with Sentinel infra?
[03:09] Liam O'Connor: yep I can do that, I'll get the initial scoping doc out by EOD Friday.
[03:13] Priya Shah: for the POC plan — I'm thinking a two-week perf-focused pilot for Aurora: synthetic load + real prompt samples, measure p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, and validate caching benefits. for Meridian, longer POC 4-6 weeks to do Private deploy, security signoffs and compliance checklist.
[03:28] Maya Torres: that sounds reasonable. two questions: one, do we need an NDA or updated data processing addendum before sharing prompt sets? and two, what pricing for POC?
[03:36] Jordan Lee: we usually do a standard DPA and we can attach a short pilot pricing schedule — often discounted or time-limited credits for POC. I'll coordinate with Legal.
[03:44] Alex Moreno: on pricing mechanics, for Aurora we'd show hosted baseline and Dedicated reserved price with a committed throughput. then show delta if they switch to private. include estimated monthly unit cost.
[03:51] Evan Kim: also we need to clarify how Redwood handles fallbacks if Dedicated capacity saturates — does traffic route to hosted and what's the data residency implication?
[03:59] Priya Shah: we have smart routing policies — we can failover to compatible model variants in hosted, but for Meridian (Private) we could not failover outside tenant boundaries without explicit approval. we'll document fallback policies per deployment.
[04:12] Alex Moreno: good point, capture as risk for Meridian.
[04:15] Maya Torres: another ask — can you provide a short benchmarking spreadsheet template so our architects can compare numbers side-by-side?
[04:21] Priya Shah: yes I'll share a template with metrics: p50/p95, tokens-per-second, cost-per-1k, cold start times, and requirements for sample data.
[04:29] Liam O'Connor: and we should have a clear handoff once POC completes — to whom on Sentinel for production procurement?
[04:35] Maya Torres: that'll be Liam for Aurora, and for Meridian it'll be our compliance lead Sarah V. I'll introduce Sarah in the intros.
[04:42] Alex Moreno: ok for next steps, I'm going to update the joint deck with the new pipeline slide and logos — send to Maya for approval. Priya will own the benchmark template. Jordan will own pilot pricing and DPA. Maya will send contact list and prompt samples.
[04:56] Evan Kim: quick competitor note — the customer mentioned cohesive pricing offers from Bedrock bundled with other AWS services; may be a procurement checkbox.
[05:04] Alex Moreno: we'll call that out in the risk column and propose an incentive for early committed capacity.
[05:09] Maya Torres: one more — for the Meridian compliance ask, do you have references or a case study we can show legal?
[05:15] Jordan Lee: we have a SOC2 + an EU residency case study, I'll attach redacted case notes and the SOC2 cert link.
[05:21] Liam O'Connor: perfect.
[05:22] Alex Moreno: anything else?
[05:25] Evan Kim: nope from me.
[05:26] Maya Torres: all good, thanks.
[05:28] Alex Moreno: wrap up — recap of next steps and timelines, we'll send minutes and next steps in an email. schedule exec sync for first week of December, Mara — sorry Maya — can you do week of 12/7?
[05:40] Maya Torres: yes week of 12/7 works.
[05:43] Alex Moreno: awesome, thanks everyone. End call.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-hears (e.g., "cohesive" vs "Cohere"), timestamps approximate.
